disposition_reason: Primary market survey printing per-product lead and cadmium concentrations for commercial grain-based and vegetable-based baby foods.

study.design: Market survey of 18 commercial baby foods (9 grain-based, 9 vegetable-based) of different brands and origins
study.origin: various international origins and local manufacture (not specified per product)
study.method: Dry ashing at 550 C for 5 h, HCl digestion, flame AAS (Shimadzu AA-7000)
study.qa: Acid-washed glassware; no CRM, recovery or blanks reported

regulatory_or_exposure.what: Limits used by the authors (Iraqi standard IQS 1103, 2020 update, and global limits)

regulatory_or_exposure.value: food intake 50 g/day, child body weight 13 kg (1-2 years); RfD Pb 0.002, Cd 0.001 mg/kg/day

unresolved: No LOD/LOQ, CRM or recovery reported; Cd values near 1 ug/kg by flame AAS are below what the technique normally detects.
Concentration formula uses V = 5 mL although digests were made up to 50 mL; possible tenfold calculation issue cannot be resolved.
Abstract says the highest Pb (1.0986 ppm) was in cereal foods, but Table 3 assigns 1.0986 to vegetable product Fv11 and the cereal maximum is 1.4363 (Fs8).
Table 5 EDI/THQ means and SDs appear transposed (e.g. EDI Pb "1.3538 ± 2.8759"); derived values, not recorded.
Whether grain-based products are dry infant cereals or ready-to-eat jars is not stated.
source_record_corrections: Printed author surname of first author is "Fadhe" in the byline (manifest: Fadhel).
